title: Whitehead theorem for spaces of CW homotopy type
statement: Use the path components and continuous based homotopy groups of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A CW complex here is a space formed from the empty space by attaching, for each $n\geq0$, a set of closed $n$-disks along their boundary spheres to the $(n-1)$-skeleton, with the weak topology for the characteristic disk maps and with the boundary of each cell contained in finitely many lower-dimensional cells. The empty space is allowed. A homotopy equivalence is a continuous map $u:A\to B$ admitting a continuous $r:B\to A$ with $ru\simeq\operatorname{id}_A$ and $ur\simeq\operatorname{id}_B$, where homotopies use ordinary product with $[0,1]$ and need not fix basepoints. Let $X,Y$ be topological spaces each homotopy equivalent to a CW complex. If a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ induces a bijection on path components and an isomorphism $\pi_n(X,x)\to\pi_n(Y,f(x))$ for every $x\in X$ and integer $n\geq1$, then $f$ is a homotopy equivalence. No connectedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.
